articles.title: Últimos feriados 2026 en el Perú: ¿Cuántos feriados hay en noviembre y diciembre?

articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.title: ¿Cómo nació el Día de la Canción Criolla y por qué se celebra en octubre?
articles.summary: Cada 31 de octubre, el Perú rinde homenaje a uno de sus mayores símbolos culturales: la música criolla. Conoce cómo nació esta celebración, desde cuándo se conmemora y por qué se convirtió en una tradición que mantiene viva la identidad y el legado musical peruano.
articles.body_text: Hay fechas que representan gran tradición e historia en nuestro país, como es el Día de la Canción Criolla. Esta festividad es capaz de reunir a toda la familia y amigos para pasar un ameno momento con el objetivo de celebrar un género musical valioso y muy escuchado por todos los peruanos. Óscar Avilés y Augusto Polo Campos son algunos de nuestro representantes más icónicos. A continuación, te vamos a contar por qué y desde cuándo se festeja. El Día de la Canción Criolla es una celebración en Perú dedicada al reconocimiento de la canción criolla, que incluye variados géneros como el vals peruano, la marinera, el huayno o el tondero, con influencias de la música española, indígena peruana y africana. El propósito de proclamar el “Día de la Canción Criolla” fue promover el arte popular y fomentar las expresiones de esta música. El 18 de octubre de 1944, el entonces jefe de Estado Manuel Prado Ugarteche, a través de una resolución suprema declaró que cada 31 de octubre se conmemore el “Día de la Canción Criolla” con el fin de difundir este género musical. La norma fue dada tras la solicitud presentada por el Centro Social Musical “Carlos A. Saco” y otras instituciones similares. El texto de la resolución señala que “el arte popular contribuye al afianzamiento de una conciencia nacionalista, por lo que conviene estimular sus manifestaciones”. Esta primera fiesta realizada en 1944 inició con el izado de la bandera peruana en los centros musicales de Lima y el Callao. Los asistentes cantaron el Himno Nacional y luego presenciaron la actuación de músicos como Teresita Arce, Carlos Pacheco, Luis Pardo y los hermanos Azcue. articles.title: Día de Muertos: conoce las fechas clave y el significado de esta tradición
articles.summary: Desde el 27 de octubre hasta el 2 de noviembre, las creencias populares mexicanas asignan un significado especial a cada jornada del Día de Muertos. Conoce a quiénes se recuerda en cada fecha, qué representan las ofrendas y cómo esta tradición mantiene vivo el recuerdo de los seres queridos fallecidos.
articles.body_text: Cada año, cuando octubre llega a sus últimos días, México se transforma en un escenario lleno de flores anaranjadas, velas encendidas y altares preparados para recordar a quienes fallecieron. El Día de Muertos es una de las expresiones culturales más representativas del país, una celebración que combina costumbres ancestrales con elementos religiosos y reúne a las familias alrededor de la memoria de sus seres queridos. Su importancia trascendió las fronteras mexicanas y, en 2008, la Unesco incorporó esta festividad a la Lista Representativa del Patrimonio Cultural Inmaterial de la Humanidad. Aunque las jornadas centrales son el 1 y 2 de noviembre, algunas creencias populares distribuyen la llegada simbólica de las almas a lo largo de varios días, desde el 27 de octubre. Cada fecha tiene una interpretación particular y está relacionada con distintos grupos de difuntos, una costumbre que explica por qué los preparativos y las ofrendas pueden variar de un hogar a otro. El calendario popular de esta festividad contempla varias fechas previas al inicio de noviembre. El 27 de octubre se asocia con las mascotas fallecidas, por lo que algunas familias colocan agua y alimentos en su memoria. Al día siguiente, el 28, se recuerda a quienes perdieron la vida en accidentes o de manera repentina; ciertas versiones de la tradición también incluyen a las llamadas ánimas solas. El 29 de octubre está dedicado, según algunas creencias, a las personas que murieron ahogadas. Para el 30, la conmemoración se extiende a las almas olvidadas o que no cuentan con familiares que las recuerden. En estos casos, algunas familias encienden velas y dejan recipientes con agua como parte de sus prácticas simbólicas. El 31 de octubre se vincula con los niños que fallecieron sin ser bautizados o que no llegaron a nacer, de acuerdo con determinadas interpretaciones populares. Posteriormente, el 1 de noviembre se recuerda a los menores fallecidos, mientras que el 2 se dedica principalmente a los adultos difuntos. Cabe precisar que este calendario no se aplica de manera uniforme en todo México: las fechas y sus significados pueden cambiar según la comunidad y las costumbres familiares. Uno de los símbolos más reconocibles de esta celebración son los altares domésticos, espacios creados para rendir homenaje a los seres queridos que ya no están. Las fotografías suelen ocupar un lugar destacado, acompañadas de veladoras, flores, papel picado y otros objetos que representan la identidad de la persona recordada. La selección de los elementos depende de las tradiciones de cada familia y, en muchos casos, de los gustos del difunto. Por ello, es habitual encontrar platillos tradicionales, bebidas, dulces y otros productos que evocan momentos compartidos. El pan de muerto y las calaveras de azúcar o chocolate también forman parte de la decoración característica de numerosos altares. En algunos hogares, los preparativos comienzan durante los últimos días de octubre para tener todo listo antes de las fechas principales. De acuerdo con determinadas costumbres, las ofrendas se instalan desde la noche del 31 de octubre y permanecen durante las jornadas de celebración, aunque el momento de colocarlas y retirarlas puede variar según la localidad. El retiro del altar suele realizarse después del 2 de noviembre y algunas familias esperan hasta el día 3. Esta práctica no responde a una regla única para todo el país, sino a las formas particulares en que cada comunidad mantiene viva la tradición. Más allá de las fechas y los objetos que se colocan en las ofrendas, esta festividad constituye una oportunidad para compartir recuerdos, transmitir historias familiares y mantener presentes a quienes fallecieron. La preparación de los altares puede convertirse en una actividad colectiva en la que participan distintas generaciones, desde los mayores que explican las costumbres hasta los más jóvenes que aprenden a conservarlas. La celebración también refleja la diversidad cultural de México, donde las prácticas relacionadas con la muerte tienen raíces indígenas y se entrelazan con tradiciones católicas. Por ello, no existe una sola manera de conmemorar el Día de Muertos: cada región aporta sus propios rituales, sabores y expresiones artísticas. En conjunto, estas manifestaciones mantienen vigente una festividad cuyo propósito central es honrar la memoria de los difuntos y fortalecer los lazos que permanecen entre las familias.

articles.title: Caso Liceo Naval: archivo contra cuatro adolescentes no es definitivo y puede ser apelado
articles.summary: El proceso continúa para los otros seis estudiantes implicados. Así avanza en el fuero judicial este caso.
articles.body_text: Tras la decisión de la Fiscalía de Familia de archivar la investigación contra cuatro adolescentes investigados, conversamos con especialistas para entender qué sigue en este caso de presunta agresión sexual contra un estudiante del Liceo Naval. El documento que informaba la decisión, señalaba que “al no haberse demostrado la responsabilidad de los adolescentes (...) por falta de elementos de convicción suficientes, procede el archivamiento, dejándose a salvo la posibilidad de reabrirse esta investigación si aparecen nuevos elementos de convicción”. Pero el caso Liceo Naval está lejos de ser cerrado. Las investigaciones y diligencias continúan para los otros seis estudiantes que actualmente permanecen recluidos en el centro juvenil Maranguita de San Miguel. Sobre ellos aún se continúa determinando las responsabilidades, con audiencias de esclarecimiento con testigos y peritos. La idea es definir el grado de participación de cada uno, la medida socioeducativa -que puede llegar hasta seis años- y la reparación civil. Dos abogados penalistas nos dan su punto de vista para entender qué seguirá en este caso. Para la abogada Jackeline López, este archivo no es definitivo, ya que la parte agraviada puede impugnarlo con un recurso de elevación de actuados, en un plazo de cinco días hábiles desde la notificación. Ella señala que la base para esta decisión podría haber sido la declaración del agraviado en la cámara Gesell y los elementos que lo corroboran. “Lo que se tiene pendiente es con relación a estos seis investigados y la eventual responsabilidad o infracción a la ley penal o medida socioeducativa que les va a corresponder. Esto conforme a la misma norma puede ser de hasta seis años en ese sentido, además de las responsabilidades civiles que se van a tener que atribuir, le corresponderá a este juzgado de familia, indicar individualmente a quién le corresponderá la responsabilidad y cuál es el grado de participación que habrían tenido”, indicó López. Por último, la abogada indicó que el Liceo Naval Almirante Guise podría ser un tercero civilmente responsable, aunque esto sería de manera solidaria, siempre y cuando alguien lo solicite ante el juzgado. Si nadie lo pide, no se incorpora. Además, señaló la necesidad de que organismos como la UGEL y el Minedu realicen una labor de control mucho más activa, a fin de evitar que hechos como este se repitan. Para el abogado penalista Vladimir Padilla, es importante aclarar que esta investigación contra menores se rige por el Código de los Niños y Adolescentes y no por el proceso penal común. Además, señala que el archivo de la investigación contra cuatro de los implicados no debilita la teoría del caso, sino que, por el contrario, la ratifica. “Lo que debemos entender es que la Fiscalía ya ha considerado que estas personas no deberían continuar siendo investigadas, sino pasar a tener la condición de testigos. Es decir, está señalando que no habrían tenido participación en los hechos y que, por el contrario, corresponde que mantengan su posición como testigos”, indicó el especialista. “Creo que, si desde un inicio se determinaba que no habían tenido participación en los hechos, debieron ser apartados de la investigación con anterioridad. Si su situación era la de testigos, esa condición debió aclararse desde el inicio”, señaló Padilla. Finalmente, el abogado cree que debe de darse “una dedicación exclusiva a este caso, no solamente en el Ministerio Público, sino también en el Poder Judicial, para esclarecer y determinar responsabilidades”.

articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.title: Pixel 11 Pro Fold: Sturdy rectengale in a wide wide world | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Google made a sturdy phone, but there is increasing competition in the foldable world.
articles.body_text: It’s strange to write this review when the world is focused on the passport-sized iPhone Duo, and China-based companies are busy releasing wide foldables with a similar design. Google, however, stuck to its guns this year and produced a Pixel 11 Pro Fold, which is pretty much similar to last year’s foldable. The changes involve a lighter design, a brighter display, better wireless charging, and an updated camera sensor. The new olive color looks subtle but gorgeous, so that’s a bonus. However, with all the options out there, the device might not attract people who might be looking to buy their first foldable — unless they’re serious Pixel fans. Nonetheless, I have enjoyed using the device because the Pixel 11 Pro Fold’s cameras are competent enough, even if they aren’t a match for the Pixel 11 Pro’s setup, and the screen is nice to use despite the very visible crease. The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is 5mm thick when unfolded (vs 5.2mm of the Pixel 10 Pro Fold) and 10.1mm thick when folded (vs 10.8 mm of the Pixel 10 Pro Fold). This one is for the spec sheet because you might not feel as much difference. Despite this, the phone is not as thin as a device like the Honor V6 Magic. The difference you might notice — if you hold both this year’s and last year’s foldables — is that the new device is 19 grams lighter. But if you are buying a new device or switching from another foldable, it’s barely noticeable. The Pixel 10 Pro Fold was already a sturdy device. With this year’s version, the company claims to have increased durability by three times. Plus, there is a new glass-ceramic cover and a glass-fiber composite back cover to take up any impact. My Pixel 10 fell a few times from the table and from my pocket, but there wasn’t any visible dent or scratch. Well done, Google. One drawback of a strong hinge is that you can’t unfold the 11 Pro Fold with one hand, and that’s by design. The outer display is ever so slightly bigger, but the more observable change is the 3,600-nit display that is an upgrade from last year’s 3,000-nit peak display. This means that you can use the phone in bright conditions better. Google’s foldable still has a very visible crease in an age where phone makers like Oppo and Honor have managed to reduce the visibility significantly. The crease is more pronounced in bright light, given there is no reflective display on the device. On the back, there is the new HiLight indicator, which still lights up only for calls from your favourite contacts, and when you are talking with Gemini hands-free. There isn’t much to talk about this feature beyond that. Reading and watching videos on a foldable is still fun, though a wide foldable might show an edge on videos. The multitasking is good, but you can only open two apps side by side. Some apps that are tuned for foldable are great to use. For instance, Gmail, being a Google app, lets you see your inbox on one side and a particular email on the other. This can help you get through emails faster. However, Slack doesn’t have this split view, and it’s frustrating because we have been through many cycles of Android foldables with apps still not suited for the expanded screen. Given how quick Apple developer system moves, Android might feel it’s lagging in foldable experiences after the iPhone Duo is out. The camps are divided as to how apps look on Duo’s unfolded phone, but developers are rapidly updating their apps to fit the unfolded screen.

articles.title: Exclusive: Here’s what 'renoa' — the first new fiber in 25 years — feels like | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Startup Everbloom's new material, renoa, is the first new fiber in 25 years, and it feels very familiar.
articles.body_text: Sometimes it seems like everyone — and every occasion — demands cashmere these days. Numerous brands sell cashmere sweaters, from Bruno Cucinelli’s $7,900 cable knit cardigan to Quince’s $50 crewneck . Menswear company Loro Piana has made cashmere a cornerstone of its lineup, helping to drive the LVMH division’s valuation above €11 billion . There are even cashmere running shirts . But as cashmere has spread throughout the fashion industry, it’s not for everyone. It’s still relatively expensive, hard to care for, and environmental fraught. The goats that produce cashmere have been trashing rangelands across Central Asia. That may change, though. I recently experienced an alternative fiber called renoa, developed by a startup called Everbloom , that’s washable and promises to be more affordable. It could bring the cashmere experience, via a substitute material, to more products and people. Renoa is made from sources of waste protein, including cashmere and wool scraps as well as down and feather “lint” leftover from the bedding industry. Everbloom processes the waste into a powder and blends it with a biodegradable biopolymer, and the combination is then extruded to the right length and diameter to mimic specific natural fibers. Renoa was recently approved as the first new fiber classification in 25 years by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, which regulates fiber labeling in the U.S. Everbloom has been developing the new fiber for three years, and is currently in the process of scaling up. The startup developed its own AI model for material science, and a cashmere substitute is the first product. Last month, I stopped by Everbloom’s headquarters in New York City, which sits 15 floors above 5 th Avenue, kitty corner from Bryant Park. There, co-founder and CEO Sim Gulati walked me through a range of products made with its company’s cashmere-like renoa, including a crewneck sweater, a pair of knit gloves, and a scarf. The sweater and gloves were soft and light, but the scarf was the most notable. It didn’t look like much, but it had been through the kind of hell and back that a pure cashmere scarf wouldn’t survive. It was a custom item that Everbloom had knit to test renoa, and Gulati had been wearing and washing it for months, including a trip through the tumble dryer before I saw it. It wasn’t pilled, and Gulati said it hadn’t shrunk, either. Everbloom is currently working with a range of companies to get renoa into consumer products. The first are likely to feature renoa as a blended fiber, making up around 20% of the material in a cashmere sweater, for example. The first product is expected to hit the market in the second quarter of 2027 Gulati said. The 80/20 cashmere-renoa blend that I felt was extremely close to the real thing, and Gulati said that additional finishing that accompanies commercial garments should eliminate any differences without compromising the washability and stability of the garment. After my visit, I kept thinking about various items in my closet that could benefit from those features. When renoa lands on shelves next year, I’ll be keeping an eye out for it. articles.title: Data centers are now a midterm issue, even in Brooklyn | TechCrunch
articles.summary: At a Brooklyn midterm party five days before Election Day, every conversation, from a council member’s fireside chat to a debate about the Democratic Party, kept circling back to AI and data centers.
articles.body_text: On Thursday evening, I slipped on my neon yellow heels and a floral mini dress. It’s New York, so I can wear whatever I want to a midterm election event full of media types, techies, policy advocates, and, well, does anyone else even exist at these things? I walked into the dimly blue-lit Brooklyn warehouse and was surprised to see the room already filling up. Newsreel, the media company founded by former Forbes and Newsweek reporter Jack Brewster, hosted the event, and the lineup was heavy-hitting. Kenneth Schlenker, co-founder of the focus app Opal, sat down for a fireside chat about “the state of attention,” and Aryan Banjan, who built the campaign management software Barza, gave a midterm forecast. I, meanwhile, was moderating a panel on data centers. Brewster said the goal was for people to “put their phones away and talk to each other about the election, five days out.” As the evening progressed, however, one topic consumed nearly every conversation: AI, data centers, and the backlash against the growing technocracy. Lately, as a tech reporter, I’ve noticed a growing chasm between tech and everyone else. I spend most of my days talking to people who see the benefits of AI, who are so ambitious in building it and so optimistic that it will succeed that, when I talk to people beyond the tech world, I forget how ugly it all seems to them. Outside the tech bubble, data centers and AI have become such an intense ballot-box issue that they could sway some midterm races on November 3. A recent report from Data Center Watch found that almost $200 billion in data center projects were delayed, stalled, or blocked in the first half of 2026 due to political and community opposition. Meanwhile, states like Pennsylvania, Georgia, Texas, New York, and Virginia are considering more guardrails and transparency around data centers’ rapid development. Hundreds of new data centers are planned in Virginia alone, a state already nicknamed the “data center capital of the world.” A fireside chat with New York City Council member Chi Ossé, just before my panel, set the tone. AI came up near the end; Ossé said he doesn’t really use it. To me, though, he didn’t seem to be for or against it. He mostly emphasized that he would like to see tech executives held more accountable and trillionaires like Elon Musk taxed more. He described himself as a democratic socialist, but a “law and order” one. When CEOs talk about a technology that could deplete 10% of human civilization, he said, “they should be called to testify in front of Congress.” My panel was up next. I moderated a discussion with Maia Woluchem, a technology and human rights researcher, and Hilary Flint, an environmental and public health advocate, about data centers. As I took the stage, I decided to get a better read on the crowd. I asked, “Who here is pro-AI data center?” and was promptly booed. Our conversation covered a range of topics and emotions. People are upset that big tech companies appear to be cutting secret deals with local officials to build billion-dollar data centers. In some cases, zoning rules make it unclear what is being built until it’s too late to protest. At the same time, people are struggling with the cost of living and doing everything they can to hold onto what’s left of the American Dream, while tech leaders talk about AI replacing workers, or even humanity itself. Residents feel they have lost control over what happens in their communities, and they worry about the environmental and health risks. The panel agreed that data centers are the physical embodiment of people’s fears and anger toward the tech class and the rapid pace of technology. “What is a life worth?” Flint said when I brought up the benefits that some communities have seen from data center build-outs. People still protest, she said, because they “value their lives a little bit more than a temporary check.” The panel after mine featured NewsNation host Batya Ungar-Sargon; political strategist Morris Katz, who worked on Zohran Mamdani’s campaign; and Vox’s Astead Herndon. They were supposed to be talking about the future of the Democratic Party. But once again, the conversation shifted to data centers. Ungar-Sargon noted that some labor unions support data centers because of the jobs they promise. (Reports show that data centers create many jobs initially, but those jobs are not permanent once construction ends.) “There used to be a lot of pride in a community in the Rust Belt about very ugly, enormous buildings in their communities because everybody worked there,” she said, nodding to an earlier comment I’d made about data centers being ugly. “And they knew that building represented prosperity for themselves, stability for their children, and a future and a piece of the American dream.”

articles.title: Apple CEO says the company doesn’t ‘want to ship AI for AI’s sake’ | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Apple's new CEO defended the company's current position in the AI landscape.
articles.body_text: During a recent interview with Wired’s Steven Levy , Apple CEO John Ternus defended the company’s current position in the AI landscape. Over the past couple years, Apple has often been described as behind on AI, especially as it delayed the release of a more powerful version of Siri, which finally launched this summer . But while Ternus — a longtime Apple executive who officially became CEO at the beginning of September — acknowledged that “everyone has an opinion,” he insisted, “I really like where we’re at.” Ternus added that Apple is “absolutely going to leverage AI” in its new products, but he said, “We don’t want to ship AI for AI’s sake. When we’re doing it right, people won’t have to think about whether it was AI that made this happen or more traditional software. What matters is, did we build something that they really love?” And when Levy pressed him on whether AI might affect Apple and its ecosystem more dramatically, with agents potentially making things like apps unnecessary, Ternus replied,”That could make life really easy, I suppose, but the creation of products is a deeply human and personal thing, something that we love to do.” Buy One Pass, Get a Second Free Cover more ground at TechCrunch’s ultimate founder bootcamp of the year by bringing your co-founder or partner for free Book before the BOGO deal expires Every weekday and Sunday, you can get the best of TechCrunch’s coverage. articles.title: Judge allows NAACP lawsuit over xAI data center pollution to move forward | TechCrunch
articles.summary: An NAACP lawsuit accuses the SpaceX-owned AI company of violating the Clean Air Act.
articles.body_text: A federal judge denied a motion by xAI seeking to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit accusing the SpaceX-owned company of failing to obtain permits needed to operate the gas turbines powering its Colossus data center outside Memphis. Suing on behalf of the NAACP, the Southern Environmental Law Center said the AI company had “installed and operated at least 35 combustion turbines and other sources of air pollution at the Colossus site without ever obtaining the necessary preconstruction or operating air permits.” It also accused xAI of violating the Clean Air Act. xAI sought to have the lawsuit dismissed, claiming that the turbines are exempt from permitting requirements because they’re mobile. The company also argued that the plaintiffs did not have the standing to sue. “Because the plaintiffs have statutory standing under the Clean Air Act, because the combustion turbines are not ‘mobile sources’ under Mississippi’s [State Implementation Plan], and because the citizen suit provision does not violate Article II of the Constitution or the private nondelegation doctrine, the plaintiffs’ claims will proceed,” Judge Debra M. Brown wrote in her decision . Focusing on xAI’s claim that these kinds of citizen lawsuits are unconstitutional, Judge Brown wrote, “Because citizen suit plaintiffs sue on their own behalf, in their own name, and seek penalties that redress harm to themselves, they are not exercising the federal government’s executive power.” TechCrunch has reached out to SpaceX for comment. In a statement , the NAACP’s director of environmental and climate justice Abre’ Connor described this as “another important victory in our effort to hold xAI accountable.” (A similar motion to dismiss from the Department of Justice was denied earlier this month ) “The courts have repeatedly rejected attempts by xAI and the DOJ to dismiss the NAACP’s Clean Air Act case, affirming our right to pursue justice for communities impacted by pollution,” Connor said. “Our position has been clear: xAI cannot operate gas turbines without the required permits.” The NAACP lawsuit is moving forward as public opinion seems to have turned sharply against data centers, with New York recently passing a moratorium on new data centers and other state and local governments considering similar measures. The backlash also prompted Amazon and Microsoft to promise to stop using NDAs in their dealings with government agencies, and it could be a significant factor in the imminent U.S. midterm elections . articles.title: OpenAI reportedly lowers funding target for new round | TechCrunch
articles.summary: OpenAI’s latest funding round doesn't seem to be living up to expectations.
articles.body_text: OpenAI’s latest funding round isn’t quite living up to expectations, according to multiple news reports. OpenAI was previously reported to be raising $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation , and then at a $1.25 trillion valuation , ahead of a planned IPO. But The Financial Times reported Friday that the company has subsequently lowered its funding target to $20 billion, with a first close that’s expected to be even lower than that. The round will be led by a group of investors from the United Arab Emirates, the FT said. A subsequent retail offering for wealthy individuals could bring the total funding amount to the $20 billion target. A follow-up story in The Wall Street Journal offered more details, namely that the company has secured $11 billion so far, and that its fundraising efforts had met with a “tepid” response from some large investors. TechCrunch has reached out to OpenAI for comment. The company’s reported funding challenges could be blamed, in part, on bad timing, as Wall Street investors have become wary of heavy AI infrastructure spending , leading to a major sell off of tech stocks. articles.title: From restaurant guides to payments, here’s how TikTok is building a super app | TechCrunch
articles.summary: TikTok may be working to become the app that people use for most of their digital activities.
articles.body_text: TikTok announced this week that it’s adding an in-app restaurant guide , marking another step in the platform’s expansion beyond social media. The company has also recently been spotted developing a feature that would allow users to send money over direct messages. The social media app has steadily expanded its offerings in recent years, adding TikTok Shop, a map for local discovery, more robust search features, games, and more. It appears that TikTok is taking steps to evolve into a “super app,” a single platform where users can do much more than just watch and share videos and that can actually handle a wide range of needs in one destination. The super app model is big in China with apps like WeChat, which is kind of like Facebook, WhatsApp, Apple Pay, and an app store all rolled into a single platform. Of course, there’s the question of whether a super app model would work outside of China, but that doesn’t mean TikTok won’t try. Instead of switching between apps, TikTok is working to become the app that people use for most of their digital activities. After taking its biggest leap with TikTok Shop, the company — which, notably, transitioned to new, primarily U.S. ownership back in January — has applied the same playbook to recent developments. TikTok has become a popular destination for restaurant recommendations, with viral videos often driving customers to local eateries. Now, the platform is looking to make that discovery process even easier with a new feature called “ Must Eat .” The community-driven guide highlights restaurants getting attention on the platform. “Must Eat” draws on more than 40 million posts and comments to compile restaurant recommendations and curated lists in one place. Users can browse restaurants by city and narrow their search by cuisine, price, rating, and location. The move puts TikTok in more direct competition with platforms like Yelp and Google Maps. It also reflects how the app is expanding its role in users’ everyday decisions, from what they buy to where they choose to go out to eat. Bloomberg reported in August that TikTok is developing a feature that would allow users to send each other money via direct messages. If rolled out, the feature would use the social media service’s TikTok Pay offering, which is already available in Southeast Asia for TikTok Shop purchases. Additionally, Reuters reported in March that TikTok had applied to Brazil’s central bank for approval to operate as a financial technology company offering lending and payment services. TikTok’s potential expansion into payments marks a significant way that the company is branching out beyond a social media platform and into a digital ecosystem. By aiming to bring financial services into its app, TikTok is looking to increase user engagement, open new revenue streams, and position itself to compete with fintech startups and e-commerce platforms. Over the years, TikTok has steadily been looking to become a place where users can come for sports highlights and content. In early June, the company launched a dedicated hub for the FIFA World Cup where users can see scores, match schedules, standings, trending videos, highlights, videos from players, and more. If people are already watching videos on TikTok but want to keep up with the score, they can do so without leaving the app or opening a dedicated sports news app or Google.

articles.title: I took two iPhones on vacation. The Duo won me over. | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The iPhone Duo has its frustrations, but it’s also fun and engaging enough that I didn’t want to switch back to my Pro Max.
articles.body_text: “I think I’m going to switch back to my other iPhone.” I’ll admit, I said this multiple times during my five-day vacation with the new iPhone Duo, after encountering frustrations with broken apps, unfamiliar gestures (a return to Touch ID, argh !), and camera concerns that had me lugging around two phones. By the time the trip was over, I didn’t want to go back. When I first unboxed the Duo, a loaner from Apple, I was genuinely intrigued. I felt a flutter of anticipation as I peeled back the factory seal wrap and booted up the device. In retrospect, this was probably the first signal that Duo was going to ultimately win me over. As a tech reporter, I’ve received a lot of test devices over the years, so unfortunately, opening a package with a new gadget inside is no longer the thrill it used to be. But sometime in the days leading up to the Duo’s ship date, I found myself actually wanting one – I had started doing the math and comparing upgrade options that would allow me to afford the $2K the phone would cost. I started scrolling TikTok reviews of Duo cases . I hesitated not only because of the price but because moving to the Duo is a major change – especially coming from an iPhone 17 Pro Max. The phones could not be more different. As I was about to head out on vacation when the Duo arrived, I decided to tote my 17 Pro Max with me too, as something of a safety net. I ended up using the Duo more, and grew comfortable with it over the course of the trip, despite some frustrations. There’s always a psychological switching cost in changing phones, but particularly going from a high-end phone to a more experimental device like the Duo. For someone used to the iPhone’s long-perfected tech and thin rectangular shape, the Duo’s short, squat, and decidedly novel nature was somewhat off-putting at first. “Where is all that screen real estate I used to have?” I lamented. “Will this thing even fit comfortably in my pocket?” As it turns out, it does. Front and back pockets, in fact. Even while wearing a case. You can sit down with it in your back pocket, effectively squashing it, and it does not break. (I meant to be more careful, but I forgot to be, repeatedly, as I tend to carry phones in my back pocket when walking around. I sat on the phone countless times. It’s clearly not that fragile.) I also dropped the phone (by accident!) at least three times. Twice from about table height and once when it got pushed off the side of the bed. It did not fall on soft carpet, but rather on concrete, tile, and wood floors. It didn’t break then either, and the screen didn’t crack. I wouldn’t call these professional drop tests by any means, but it certainly was a relief for someone fairly clumsy with their phone. Of course, I did encounter some frustrations. I had to scroll more to read back through text threads because of the Duo’s small outer screen; unoptimized apps with numerous controls sometimes had key features tucked away in a “more” (three-dot) menu, leading to a hunt to find the option you needed; and, on multiple occasions, the Google Search app just froze. Though not Apple’s fault, the latter turned out to be my biggest annoyance software-wise, given that Search is one of my go-to apps especially when traveling. On vacation, I open the app repeatedly to look up points of interest, restaurant reviews, distances between towns, weather, and more. But Google’s app would just stop working, and tapping its back button did nothing.

articles.title: Pile-ins, payouts, and pacing pressure: the investors behind the VCs open up | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The money behind the money is thrilled, mostly.
articles.body_text: The limited partners who provide the capital to venture firms — the “money behind the money” — are feeling great right now. They’re in uncharted territory in many ways, but also potentially exceedingly lucrative territory. Normally, LPs typically spread their bets across many firms to diversify their own portfolios. They write checks to emerging managers and established ones, to generalist firms and specialists. The goal is a strong return, but also to minimize risk. That’s the typical playbook. But typical is out the window. OpenAI and Anthropic’s valuations have shot up so quickly that nearly everyone has piled into the same two companies on the way up, often inside the same venture firm, despite the longstanding venture convention of avoiding investments that conflict with one another. No one is complaining, either. The LPs I speak with seem unbothered by this big gamble, given the potential returns; they’re expecting a bonanza. But they do see danger ahead, even if they describe this as a “yellow light” situation, and they’re uneasy about how quickly VCs are coming back to raise new funds. I talked about all of it recently with Beezer Clarkson of LGT Capital Partners, a Zurich-based diversified asset manager, and Amit Bhatti of TrueBridge, a Chapel Hill firm that focuses solely on venture. This conversation has been edited for length. These are strange days — exciting but also scary. How are you feeling about your roles right now, and your place in this startup ecosystem? Beezer Clarkson: It’s very busy, but I wouldn’t say it’s scary. There’s a lot of change and a lot of variables at play. I love venture, so I find the chaos fun. I’ve been doing this for a couple of decades, so seeing the cycles makes it less scary. You appreciate that these things happen, and that we should enjoy the upside, because sometimes there’s downside, and the up is a lot more fun than the down. Amit Bhatti: If anything, it’s exciting. Venture is sometimes looked at as a niche, and now that AI is all-consuming, all the attention is on venture. This feels like our moment more than it is like, “Oh gosh, what’s going to happen?” The pace of investing and the valuations may be different, but really meaningful stuff is happening, and all the attention is focused on this corner of private equity. Your funds all hold the same brands now, OpenAI and Anthropic, multiplied across however many funds you back, and your job is to keep your institutions diversified. How do you think about that? Obviously it’s great right now, but if things turned, it would be less great. Amit Bhatti: Venture has always been a power law business, so I actually view the concentration as a good thing. If we were getting to the maturity of one of our funds and there were still lots of tiny positions, something’s gone wrong. Our funds that are 10-plus years old are starting to consolidate into a few names. There’s a lot of Databricks, a lot of SpaceX, a lot of Stripe. In this generation of funds, I would hope there’s a lot of Anthropic and a lot of OpenAI. That’s a feature, not a bug. Not every one of these companies is going to work out, but that consolidation is typical. What’s different is how quickly it’s happened. I don’t view it as an immediate panic signal. Beezer Clarkson: At the early stage, you still see quite a diversity of opportunity sets, and the dollars are smaller. It aggregates up into the same companies, but early-stage funds obviously aren’t doing the big late-stage stuff, so you have more diversity there, if that’s what you’re looking for. Funds that invested on four-year cycles have shrunk that to three, then two, then 18 months. Is the pacing okay, or is it concerning?

articles.title: Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Big Tech is pouring billions into AI infrastructure, but mounting debt, negative cash flow, and growing investor skepticism are raising questions about the sustainability of the AI spending boom.
articles.body_text: Investors are getting nervous about AI infrastructure spending just as the Big Tech companies double down. Over the past two weeks, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft have outlined plans to spend more than $740 billion on capital expenditures this year, which Wall Street is reading as AI infrastructure spending, including data centers and chips. Earlier in the AI boom, investors largely rewarded such big outlays, viewing them as a sign of confidence in the technology’s growth potential. But as we enter the fourth quarter, that enthusiasm seems to be giving way to concerns about negative free cash flow (spending more cash than a company brings in), mounting debt, and whether these enormous investments will ever generate enough returns. The anxiety spilled across the market on Friday. The Nasdaq fell 2.9%, and chip stocks took a drubbing, too: Nvidia dropped 4%, Broadcom more than 5%, and Qualcomm 11%. Alphabet, which plummeted 12% on Thursday, its worst day on record, wiping out $500 billion in market value, fell again. A big part of the concern is that companies that used to have overflowing free cash flow from their core businesses are getting hit as AI threatens the economics of those businesses. Alphabet provided the clearest example of that this week. Google’s parent company reported negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion in the third quarter, its second consecutive quarter in the red, even as quarterly capex grew to $51.4 billion. Alphabet expects to spend up to $205 billion this year, and expects that spending to keep rising in 2027. Meanwhile, the wild success of AI Mode — Google’s AI-powered chatbot feature built directly into Search — is eating into the company’s money-maker. Google’s Search advertising business, which makes up roughly half of its revenue, saw growth slow to 12%, its weakest pace in five quarters. That leaves Google walking a tightrope. It’s spending billions on the AI technology that could undermine the search business that pays it. Amazon is in a similar boat after reporting negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion over the past 12 months, compared with $14.8 billion in positive free cash flow the year before. The company says it expects to spend $220 billion in capex this year. Even though revenue at its cloud business, AWS, grew 39%, Amazon’s stock tumbled 7% after it reported earnings Thursday. Meta is also burning cash, reporting negative free cash flow of $2.1 billion in the third quarter as capex outpaced its operating cash. It’s guiding to as much as $145 billion in capex this year. The company noted that Muse, its new free personal AI agent, is a bit of a money pit (it’s “very compute-intensive to run,” CEO Mark Zuckerberg has said). But ad revenue grew 26%. Still, no amount of good news saved Meta from taking a 10% hit on its stock last week. Microsoft was the only exception when it came to free cash flow — it recorded $18.6 billion in positive free cash flow in its latest quarter, with spending on capex at $45.2 billion, less than the $50 billion it projected. Microsoft said that wasn’t an intentional pullback from AI spending, blaming delays in capacity from third-party providers. As a result, shares of smaller companies that rent out AI computing power sank . It’s worth noting that the money to pay for all of this AI infrastructure isn’t just coming from the Big Tech companies’ profits. It’s also showing up in stock and bond sales. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Oracle raised a combined $326 billion in debt in 2026, triple the amount raised last year. Demand for AI compute remains strong. Google, Amazon, and Microsoft all saw gains in their cloud businesses. But investors are getting spooked by the costs of meeting that demand. These muddied waters could complicate Anthropic’s highly anticipated IPO. The AI company filed to go public earlier this week, and its future growth depends on securing enormous amounts of compute. Financial Times reported Friday that Blackstone has warned investors the company might not qualify for an investment-grade rating after its IPO, meaning it might end up being more reliant on the hyperscalers and third-parties to fund its infrastructure ambitions.

articles.title: Binance will buy FTX after liquidity crisis rumors
articles.summary: The world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance, has signed a nonbinding letter to acquire the third-largest exchange, FTX. The agreement comes after Twitter beef between the founders.
articles.body_text: Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange by volume, has signed a letter of intent to buy competitor FTX, the third-largest exchange by volume. The acquisition came after a CoinDesk article prompted speculation about FTX’s balance sheet. The terms of the deal weren’t disclosed. The letter of intent is nonbinding, and Binance CEO Changpeng “CZ” Zhao said the firm will conduct due diligence before the acquisition. Binance’s acquisition came after CZ said on Sunday he’d sell FTX’s FTT token, leading to a plunge in the token’s value. That token was the biggest asset on the balance sheet of Alameda Research, the trading firm also founded by Sam Bankman-Fried, the CEO of FTX, according to CoinDesk’s story. Bankman-Fried said yesterday that CZ’s Binance was attempting to target FTX “with false rumors.” Today, Bankman-Fried said that “rumors in media of conflict between our two exchanges” were exaggerated and that the Binance acquisition will help clear out a backlog of customer withdrawals. Earlier this year, Bankman-Fried rescued BlockFi and Voyager Digital, two troubled crypto lenders that were under threat of bank runs. He’s also cozied up to US lawmakers, donating more than $39 million in this election cycle — still less than he’d promised, which was $1 billion before 2024. By contrast, CZ’s Binance has been targeted by regulators in dozens of countries, including the US. The Securities and Exchange Commission and the Department of Justice in the US are both probing Binance, according to The Wall Street Journal. The deal between the two companies isn’t totally done. “This is a highly dynamic situation, and we are assessing the situation in real time,” CZ said on Twitter. People pulled $1.4 billion from FTX on the Ethereum blockchain over the last day, according to The Wall Street Journal.

articles.title: Harley-Davidson spins out LiveWire as its own electric motorcycle brand
articles.summary: Harley-Davidson is spinning out its electric motorcycle division as a standalone company called LiveWire. A new electrified model will be unveiled in July.
articles.body_text: LiveWire, the first electric motorcycle from Harley-Davidson, will now become its own standalone brand. The Milwaukee-based company announced that it would be spinning out its electric motorcycle division as its own company with a distinct lineup and a tailored retail experience. Harley-Davidson plans to unveil the “first LiveWire branded motorcycle” on July 8th to coincide with the International Motorcycle Show. It’s a similar move to how Harley-Davidson approached its new electric bicycle company, Serial 1. The idea is that LiveWire continues to benefit from its relationship with its parent company while also forging its own brand identity that is distinct from Harley-Davidson. It’s a shift from how the company approached its current LiveWire model, in which the Harley-Davidson logo is front and center, while the LiveWire brand is practically nonexistent. And it’s a sign that going forward, Harley-Davidson is interested in letting its electrified models stand on their own terms. “With the mission to be the most desirable electric motorcycle brand in the world, LiveWire will pioneer the future of motorcycling, for the pursuit of urban adventure and beyond,” Jochen Zeitz, chairman, president, and CEO of Harley-Davidson, said in a statement. “LiveWire also plans to innovate and develop technology that will be applicable to Harley-Davidson electric motorcycles in the future.” [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/22504479/3_LiveWire_Black_CMYK_PRIMARY_LOCKUP.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] There’s a new logo and a new “virtual” headquarters, with engineering teams stationed in Silicon Valley and Milwaukee. LiveWire will work with Harley-Davidson dealerships as an independent brand, with a blend of digital and physical retail formats. Asked whether this will include online ordering, a Harley-Davidson spokesperson responded with a cautiously worded statement. “It depends on the state in which you live,” the spokesperson said. “LiveWire is creating a purchase path that allows us to meet the expectations for a digital-first purchase experience, supported by a network of committed dealers that allow customers to choose their path and engagement model.” The question is whether this branding strategy will lead to better sales for Harley-Davidson’s electric models. Last year, Reuters reported that the company’s plan to appeal to a younger generation of motorcyclists with the LiveWire was struggling, with most of the preorders coming from older or preexisting customers. Harley-Davidson’s overall sales have been stagnant lately after hitting a low point in 2018. The problem could be that the price, which starts at $29,799, isn’t that much cheaper than a Tesla Model 3. Dealers told Reuters that many younger customers were turned off by the price tag. Harley-Davidson is also facing some stiff competition from rivals like Zero Motorcycles, which recently teamed up with power sports manufacturer Polaris on a new lineup of electric-powered ATVs and snowmobiles. And as the broader world of transportation shifts to electric, the company will be under increasing pressure from its shareholders to prove its vision for the future can be profitable.

Google’s new Jules AI agent will help developers fix buggy code
articles.summary: Google has announced an experimental AI-powered code agent called “Jules” that uses Gemini 2.0 to automatically fix Python and Javascript coding errors.
articles.body_text: Google has announced an experimental AI-powered code agent called “Jules” that can automatically fix coding errors for developers. Jules was introduced today alongside Gemini 2.0, and uses the updated Google AI model to create multi-step plans to address issues, modify multiple files, and prepare pull requests for Python and Javascript coding tasks in GitHub workflows. Microsoft introduced a similar experience for GitHub Copilot last year that can recognize and explain code, alongside recommending changes and fixing bugs. Jules will compete against Microsoft’s offering, and also against tools like Cursor and even Claude and ChatGPT’s coding abilities. Google’s launch of a coding-focused AI assistant is no surprise — CEO Sundar Pichai said in October that more than a quarter of all new code at the company is now generated by AI. “Jules handles bug fixes and other time-consuming tasks while you focus on what you actually want to build,” Google says in its blog post. “This effort is part of our long-term goal of building AI agents that are helpful in all domains, including coding.” Developers have full control to review and adjust the plans created by Jules, before choosing to merge the code it generates into their projects. The announcement doesn’t say that Jules will spot bugs for you, so presumably it needs to be directed to a list of issues that have already been identified to fix. Google also says that Jules is in early development and “may make mistakes,” but internal testing has shown it’s been beneficial for boosting developer productivity and providing real-time updates to help track and manage tasks. Jules is launching today for a “select group of trusted testers” according to Google, and will be released to other developers in early 2025. Updates about availability and how development is progressing will be available via the Google Labs website.

articles.title: The Nvidia AI antitrust investigation is ‘escalating,’ reports Bloomberg
articles.summary: Nvidia and other companies have received subpoenas indicating a Department of Justice antitrust investigation into its AI chip business is moving forward.
articles.body_text: An antitrust investigation by the Department of Justice focusing on Nvidia’s AI dominance as the hardware company of choice is escalating, reports Bloomberg. The outlet reports that Nvidia and other companies have received legally binding requests for information as its sources say regulators are investigating whether Nvidia is “making it harder to switch to other suppliers and penalizes buyers that don’t exclusively use its artificial intelligence chips.” “Nvidia wins on merit, as reflected in our benchmark results and value to customers, and customers can choose whatever solution is best for them. We have inquired with the U.S. Department of Justice and have not been subpoenaed. Nonetheless, we are happy to answer any questions regulators may have about our business,” said Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo, as reported previously by CNBC. Earlier this summer, Nvidia had overtaken Microsoft as the world’s most valuable company, but now it trails both Microsoft and Apple. Before the subpoenas were reported on Tuesday afternoon, its share price dropped more than 9 percent, wiping out about $279 billion in market value in one day. But as Bloomberg notes, Nvidia’s stock is still up more than double this year as the AI boom has fueled sales of the company’s pricey chips, even after a report by The Information a few weeks ago saying that its upcoming Blackwell series of AI chips may be delayed “by three months or more due to design flaws.” Update, September 4th: Added Nvidia statement previously reported by CNBC.

Större delen av pengarna kom från den utpressade mannen. articles.body_text: Sex meter under marken grävdes tunneln rakt in i EU. Avslöjandet vid Litauens hårdbevakade gräns mot Belarus visar hur hybridkriget trappas upp – med tunnlar, smugglare, migranter och misstänkta infiltratörer. Expressen har följt en litauisk gränspatrull i den utsatta zonen, omgiven av Belarus på tre sidor. Det här är både EU:s och Natos yttre gräns. Ett fyra meter högt metallstängsel. Taggtråd. Larm. Övervakningskameror med 70 meters mellanrum. Värmekameror. Sensorer i marken. Tungt beväpnade patruller med hundar, drönare och antidrönarvapen. De baltiska länderna rustar mot hybridattacker och andra angrepp från Ryssland och Belarus , som riskerar att underminera EU och Nato. Samtidigt växer Baltic Defence Line fram längs den östra flanken – den militära försvarslinjen med stridsvagnshinder, förberedelser för att kunna spränga broar och annan infrastruktur samt planer för mineringar om ett ryskt anfall skulle komma med stöd från Belarus. Parallellt bygger Polen Eastern Shield, östra skölden, en omfattande försvarslinje av hinder som ska bromsa en snabb rysk framryckning via Belarus in i EU och Nato. Ett av hoten utgörs i dag av professionella grupper som försöker gräva sig in i länderna via djupa tunnlar där gränshindren med staket och taggtråd inte går att forcera. – Detta är en del av hybridattacker. Om du gräver tunnlar, skickar in illegala migranter eller skickar drönare handlar det inte om fred. Det handlar inte om säkerhet. Det handlar om eskalering. Så jag vet inte varför de eskalerar. Kanske försöker de skapa instabilitet i vårt samhälle och minska vårt stöd till Ukraina, säger Litauens försvarsminister Robertas Kaunas när han beskriver läget med tunnlarna som grävs från den belarusiska sidan in i Litauen och därmed också in i EU och Nato. Ett dygn senare är vi vid den utsatta gränsen mot Belarus. Expressen har följt gränsbevakningens jakt på tunnlar och människor som försöker ta sig över gränsen i ett av de mest kritiska gränsavsnitten i Litauen. Området, känt som Dieveniškės-utskottet eller ”blindtarmen”, är en litauisk ”halvö” av land som skjuter in i Belarus. Vid sin smalaste punkt är den bara fyra kilometer bred, och en väg leder in till området via en kontrollstation. Litauens gräns mot Belarus är en av EU:s och Natos yttre gränser.

En federal domare i Florida har avvisat hans stämningsansökan på 10 miljarder dollar, motsvarande cirka 100 miljarder svenska kronor, mot WSJ som undermålig, rapporterar NBC News . Tidningen publicerade vad som allt att döma är en födelsedagshälsning från Donald Trump till Jeffrey Epstein på dennes 50-årsdag 2003. Den intima hälsningen är skriven inom ramen för en tecknad kvinnokropp där Trumps autograf tycks föreställa könshår. De avslutas med den kryptiska hälsningen: ” Grattis på födelsedagen – och må varje dag bli ännu en underbar hemlighet ”. Hälsningen är en av många från vänner till Epstein som ingår i ett födelsedagsalbum som pedofilmiljardärens kumpan, Ghislaine Maxwell, sammanställt åt honom på hans födelsedag. Trump har förnekat att det är han som ligger bakom och stämde WSJ för förtal. Men eftersom presidenten inte lyckats bevisa att ont uppsåt låg bakom publiceringsbeslutet så avvisas nu stämningsansökan – för andra gången. Donald Trump lovade under sin presidentvalskampanj att offentliggöra Epsteinutredningen. Men efter att han fått makten gjorde han allt för att hålla den hemlig.

articles.title: 100 dök upp på fest – stökig hallowennatt
articles.summary: Halloweennatten blev stökig. I Malmö spårade en hemmafest ut – där ett hundratal ungdomar dök upp.
articles.body_text: I Malmö spårade en hemmafest ut – där ett hundratal ungdomar dök upp. – Det har varit mycket att göra i natt, säger polisens presstalesperson Jakob Palmgren. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Många i Sydsverige har festat för att fira in allhelgonadagen, enligt polisen. Flera anmälningar om ringa misshandel utan större skador har upprättats. – Det har varit mycket att göra i natt, och inte bara på ungdomsfester utan även på fester med vuxna människor där det har varit fylla och bråk, säger Jakob Palmgren, polisens presstalesperson. Polisen larmades bland annat till en bostad i Malmö där ett hundratal ungdomar festade. – Det var hemma hos någon där föräldrarna inte var hemma, sen hade det bara dykt upp fler och fler ungdomar, säger Jakob Palmgren. Larmet handlade initialt om ett slagsmål, som polisen kunde avvärja. På platsen fick polisen även veta att saker var tagna. – Vi upprättade en anmälan om grov stöld då en Ipad, Xbox och högtalare försvunnit från bostaden. Vissa saker har lämnats tillbaka men högtalaren ska fortfarande vara borta, säger Jakob Palmgren. På en annan ungdomsfest i Ronneby krossades ett fönster och polisen anmälde händelsen som skadegörelse. Pojken, som misstänks ha krossat rutan, fördes till sjukhus med en skada i handen. I norra Skåne blev en man puttad in i en öppen eld av två personer, enligt Kristianstadbladet . Han brännskadades och fördes till sjukhus. Polisen utreder misshandel. Polisen har även haft fullt upp i Västsverige.
